findings.title: Factory-owned queue pool is shut down by strategy close
findings.body: ResultsStrategyFactory creates a single FixedQueuePool in __init__ and passes it to every SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy. SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()/join() shuts that pool down. Arroyo recreates processing strategies on partition rebalances, so closing the old strategy permanently stops the shared workers/queues; the next strategy created for the new assignment will submit work to a shut-down pool and messages may be dropped or rejected. The pool lifecycle must be owned by the factory, or a new pool must be created per strategy.

findings.title: OffsetTracker iterates all_offsets while other threads can add partitions
findings.body: get_committable_offsets builds `list(self.all_offsets.keys())` without a lock protecting the key set. add_offset can insert a new partition key concurrently under a per-partition lock. In CPython this can raise `RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration`, causing the commit loop to fail and potentially delaying or interrupting offset commits whenever new partitions appear.

findings.title: OffsetTracker can commit past untracked offset gaps
findings.body: get_committable_offsets uses `start = max(last_committed + 1, min_offset)`. If the offset immediately after `last_committed` was never added to `all_offsets` (for example, a message skipped because it was not a BrokerValue, filtered before submit, or lost due to an error), `min_offset` jumps past that gap and later completed offsets become committable. This can commit past an unseen offset and violates the intended contiguous-offset commit guarantee.

findings.title: Workers exit instead of draining queues during shutdown
findings.body: FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets `worker.shutdown = True` and then calls `queue.shutdown(immediate=False)`. OrderedQueueWorker.run loops on `while not self.shutdown`; if shutdown is set while items remain in the queue, the worker exits after finishing its current item and leaves the rest of the queued work unprocessed. This defeats graceful draining on shutdown.

findings.title: join()/close() stop committing before draining in-flight work
findings.body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.join ignores its timeout and calls close(). close() sets the shutdown event, joins the commit thread, and then shuts down the pool. It does not wait for queues to become empty or perform a final commit after workers drain. During graceful shutdown, queued or in-flight items may be left unprocessed or processed after commits stop, so their offsets are not committed.

findings.title: Unbounded queues and no backpressure
findings.body: FixedQueuePool creates `queue.Queue()` with no maxsize, and SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.poll only emits metrics. If workers fall behind, the consumer thread can continue consuming Kafka messages and enqueueing them without bound, causing memory growth. The PR description mentions natural backpressure, but no backpressure mechanism is implemented.

findings.title: Failed work items are marked complete and can be committed
findings.body: OrderedQueueWorker catches exceptions from result processing and then calls `offset_tracker.complete_offset` in the finally block. ResultProcessor.__call__ also swallows exceptions. A message that fails processing is therefore treated as done and may be committed, dropping the result with no retry or DLQ. Transient failures can cause silent data loss.

findings.title: Uses Python 3.13-only queue shutdown APIs
findings.body: FixedQueuePool.shutdown calls `q.shutdown(immediate=False)` and workers catch `queue.ShutDown`. These APIs were added in Python 3.13. On older supported interpreters shutdown raises AttributeError (caught and logged), workers may remain blocked in `get()`, and exception matching on `queue.ShutDown` can fail. Graceful shutdown will be unreliable unless Python >= 3.13 is required.

findings.title: Commit callback is invoked from a background thread
findings.body: _commit_loop calls the Arroyo commit callback from a dedicated daemon thread. The commit callback/commit policy is normally driven by the stream processor thread, and there is no synchronization here with poll/close/join or partition rebalances. If the callback or underlying consumer state is not thread-safe, this can race and corrupt commit state or cause commits during shutdown/rebalance.

findings.title: decode_payload asserts on FilteredPayload in queue mode
findings.body: ResultsStrategyFactory.decode_payload asserts that the payload is not FilteredPayload, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy expects a decoder to return None for filtered/invalid messages. In thread-queue mode a FilteredPayload triggers AssertionError, which is caught by the strategy's generic error path and logged as an unexpected submit error before being marked complete. Filtered payloads should be handled explicitly by returning None.

findings.title: Negative max_workers creates an invalid queue pool
findings.body: FixedQueuePool is created with `num_queues=max_workers or 20`. This handles None and 0 but not negative values. A negative `--max-workers` would create no queues and later queue selection/submission would fail or behave unpredictably. max_workers should be validated to be positive.

findings.title: Error-handling test asserts behavior the implementation does not guarantee
findings.body: test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling makes processing raise and asserts that no offsets are committed. The implementation marks failed work items complete and may commit them after the commit loop's one-second interval, so the test only passes if it finishes before that commit. It is timing-dependent and validates the wrong behavior; it should deterministically assert the intended failure semantics.
